subject: obstetrics-gynaecology
title: Abnormal uterine bleeding: FIGO PALM-COEIN classification and management

steps.tx: The International Federation of Gynecology and Obstetrics classifies abnormal uterine bleeding using the **FIGO PALM-COEIN system**. This universally recognized framework categorizes etiologies into structural causes measurable by imaging or histology (Polyp, Adenomyosis, Leiomyoma, Malignancy and hyperplasia) and non-structural causes (Coagulopathy, Ovulatory dysfunction, Endometrial primary defects, Iatrogenic interventions, and Not otherwise classified).
steps.say: FIGO categorizes abnormal uterine bleeding using the PALM-COEIN system. Structural causes are Polyp, Adenomyosis, Leiomyoma, and Malignancy. Non-structural causes comprise Coagulopathy, Ovulatory dysfunction, Endometrial defects, Iatrogenic causes, and Not otherwise classified.

steps.tx: The initial evaluation of abnormal uterine bleeding mandates distinguishing acute hemorrhage from chronic irregularities. In non-pregnant reproductive-age women, pregnancy must always be excluded with **serum quantitative beta-hCG**. Detailed history determines bleeding volume, cyclicity, and systemic coagulation markers. Transvaginal ultrasonography reliably measures endometrial thickness and detects architectural distortion within the endometrial-myometrial junction.
steps.say: Evaluation starts with excluding pregnancy using beta-hCG. History assesses volume, frequency, and bleeding disorders. Transvaginal ultrasound measures endometrial thickness and identifies anatomical distortions like polyps and fibroids.

left.title: Ovulatory AUB (AUB-O)
points: Common at extremes of reproductive life (PCOS, perimenopause)

right.title: Endometrial / Structural AUB (AUB-E / L)
points: Structural distortion by polyps, fibroids or adenomyosis

steps.tx: Sampling the endometrium via outpatient biopsy is critical to rule out premalignant and malignant lesions. An **endometrial biopsy** is strongly indicated for any woman aged forty-five and older with abnormal uterine bleeding. In patients under forty-five, biopsy is mandatory if high-risk factors exist, including obesity with chronic unopposed estrogen, polycystic ovary syndrome, Lynch syndrome, or persistent bleeding despite medical therapy.
steps.say: Endometrial biopsy rules out hyperplasia and malignancy. It is mandatory for women aged forty-five and older with abnormal bleeding, and in younger women with risk factors like obesity, PCOS, Lynch syndrome, or medical therapy failure.

steps.tx: First-line medical therapy for heavy menstrual bleeding without structural pathology is the **levonorgestrel intrauterine system**. The 52-milligram LNG-IUS reduces menstrual blood loss by over ninety percent while providing highly effective contraception. Alternative non-hormonal options include tranexamic acid, an antifibrinolytic administered only during menses, and oral nonsteroidal anti-inflammatory drugs that correct local prostaglandin imbalance.
steps.say: First-line medical therapy for heavy menstrual bleeding is the levonorgestrel intrauterine system, reducing blood loss by over ninety percent. Non-hormonal alternatives include tranexamic acid taken during bleeding days, and oral anti-inflammatory drugs.
